files.filesLine: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} of {maxFiles}
files.howBody: A file is kept in a private store. Before it can be downloaded it is checked: anything that can run (macros, scripts, embedded objects), anything password-protected and anything that is not the kind of file its name says is refused and deleted. This is a check of what a file can do, not a virus scan against known malware. Only you can see or download your files, each download link works for a minute, and a file is deleted {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after it was uploaded.
files.empty: No documents yet. Choose files on the left to upload one.
files.deleteFailed: The file couldn't be deleted. Try again.
files.notLoadedBody: Your documents couldn't be loaded. Check your connection and open this step again.
files.notSetUpBody: File uploads are not set up on this server yet.
files.quotaBody: You are using {used} of {quota} and {files} of {maxFiles} files. Delete documents you no longer need to make room.
files.reason_wrong_type: its contents are not the kind of file its name says.
files.reason_too_large: it is larger than the limit, or than the size that was declared.
files.reason_encrypted: it is password-protected, so it can't be checked. Remove the password and upload it again.
files.reason_macros: it contains macros. Save it without macros and upload it again.
files.reason_active_content: it contains something that can run or fetch from elsewhere: a script, an embedded object or file, or a remote template.
files.reason_archive_bomb: it expands to far more than its size.
files.reason_unreadable: it is built in a way the check can't read. Save it again from the program that made it.
files.reason_scan_failed: the check could not be completed. Upload it again.
files.problem_bad_name: the name is empty or longer than 120 characters.
files.problem_bad_type: only PDF, Excel (.xlsx, .xls) and Word (.docx, .doc) files can be uploaded.
files.problem_quota_bytes: it would take you past {quota}. Delete a document first.
files.problem_quota_files: you already have {maxFiles} files. Delete one first.
files.problem_storage_full: the file store is full for now. Try again later.
files.problem_not_set_up: file uploads are not set up on this server.
files.problem_in_flight: wait for your other uploads to finish, then try again.
files.problem_not_expected: this file's contents have already arrived.
files.problem_busy: the server is busy with other uploads. Try again in a minute.
files.problem_too_slow: the upload took too long to arrive. Try again on a faster connection.
files.problem_not_ready: the file can be downloaded once it has passed its check.
files.problem_storage_unavailable: the file store can't be reached right now. Try again in a minute.
files.problem_send_failed: the file could not be sent. Check your connection and try again.
files.problem_scan_slow: the check is taking longer than usual. It will show here when it is done.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Variater is a tool for modelling leveraged buyouts. This page says what it keeps about you, who handles it for us, and how to have it removed.
privacy.storedSignIn: Sign-in is run by Clerk. Clerk holds your email address and, if you sign in with Google, the name and picture Google shares. Variater's own database keeps only Clerk's id for you, never your name or email address.
privacy.storedProfile: The four answers you give when you sign up: country, preferred currency, number format and time zone. And one choice: whether you want your usual figures suggested (Deal, Inputs, Starting point). The suggestions themselves are never kept: each time you open a deal they are worked out from your own saved deals in the same region and sector. Nobody else's deals are read for you, and yours are never read for anyone else. Switch it off and your deals are not read for it at all.
privacy.storedDeals: The deals you save, their earlier versions, the actual results you enter for them, and your settings. With each deal and version we keep which version of the model it was saved with and the IRR and MOIC it gave then, so reopening it can tell you if its results have changed. Nothing from a deal is ever written to a log or an error report.
privacy.storedActivity: A history of what you did and when: a deal created, edited (which fields, never the figures), renamed, archived, a version kept or restored, actual results saved, a download, a deal deleted, changes to your settings, letting a deal count in model validation or stopping it, switching suggestions of your usual figures on or off, and, for an administrator, showing or hiding the reference library and proposing, approving or rejecting a reference transaction (public filing data; the library keeps which account reviewed it). It holds no figures, deal names or version labels, so it outlives a deleted deal without keeping anything from it. A file uploaded or deleted is one line too, without the file's name.
privacy.storedFiles: The documents you upload (Deal, Documents): the file itself, in a private store only our server holds the key to, and beside it the name you gave it, its kind, its size and whether it passed its check. Nothing is read out of a file and kept, and no file name or link is ever written to a log. Each file is checked on our server before it can be downloaded; one that is refused is deleted at once.
privacy.storedCoverage: The companies you follow (Equity research, Coverage) under the names you give them, and the results you accept for them: the figures of each statement, the page each came from, and which figures you corrected or accepted as read. Nothing from a read is kept until you accept it. The figures stay when the filing itself is deleted (90 days after upload), until you remove them. Also the sector model you save for each company, with its versions, and its results note: what you type for it (your view, target, argument and date) and the linking sentences last written, never a figure (those are read from the model each time the note is drawn). Your firm's name and disclosures, typed once for your notes.
privacy.storedAddin: If you use the Excel add-in: a sign-in of its own for each time you sign the add-in in, kept only as a one-way fingerprint with the time it ends (a working day later), so the stored copy can't sign anyone in. It reaches your coverage and uploading a results PDF to read, nothing else (not your deals or your other documents), and ends when you sign the add-in out. The add-in keeps that sign-in, and the email address you signed in with, in Excel's own browser storage on your computer; the cells it writes are in your workbook, not on our server.
privacy.storedAiUsage: How much of the AI you used, a day at a time: how many results pages were read and note sentences written for you, how many requests that took, the tokens counted and what they cost (or would cost) at the AI provider's price list. Only counts and amounts, never anything from a file or from what the AI answered. Kept for 400 days, so a year of results seasons can be compared; each night the totals for everyone together are added up without naming anyone.
privacy.validation: Off unless you switch it on for a deal (Backtest, Plan and actuals). Then, each night, that deal's plan and actual results are run through the model on our server to see whether its outcome fell inside the ranges it predicted. Only counts and rates per region, sector, size and era are kept in the report everyone signed in can see: never the deal, its name, its figures or your account, and a group with fewer than five users' deals shows neither its figures nor how many it holds. Switch it off and the next report leaves the deal out; deleting the deal does the same.
privacy.google: Google shares your name, email address and profile picture with Clerk, only so that you can sign in. Variater asks for nothing else from your Google account and never reads your Google data.
privacy.companies: A company search, and loading a company's figures, sends what you typed (a name, ticker, LEI, ISIN or company number) from our server to the public registers searched: the US SEC (EDGAR), filings.xbrl.org, GLEIF, UK Companies House and Japan's EDINET. They see our server asking, never who you are. The figures are public filings, kept in a store every account shares, with nothing about who asked for them.
privacy.reader: When you ask Variater to read a results filing you uploaded (Equity research, Coverage), our server sends that file and pictures of its statement pages to Google's Gemini models, which read the figures. While the reader runs on Google's free tier, Google may use what it is sent to improve its products, so you are asked to confirm the file is a listed company's published results before anything is sent. What the models answer is kept for six hours so you can see it, then deleted; nothing from the file is written to a log. A file bigger than 13 MB is held in Google's file store for the read and deleted as soon as it is done. When you ask the AI to write a results note's linking sentences, it is sent only what each figure means and which way it moved ("revenue, current year", "higher than last year"), never the company, a figure, your view or anything from a filing.
privacy.processors: Clerk (sign-in), Vercel (the website), Render (the model API), Neon (the database, in the United States), Supabase (encrypted nightly backups, and the documents you upload), Upstash (usage counters, keyed by a one-way hash of your id), Google (reading the results filings you ask it to read, and writing a note's linking sentences when you ask), Sentry (error reports, with deal contents removed) and Better Stack (uptime checks).
privacy.not: No advertising, no selling or sharing of your data, and no tracking cookies: the only cookies are the ones that keep you signed in.
privacy.keep: Your deals, their actual results and your settings stay until you delete them or ask us to delete your account. A deleted deal's activity stays in your account's history until you ask us to delete your account; edits older than a week are merged into one line a day. An uploaded document is deleted when you delete it, and otherwise 90 days after it was uploaded. Counts of AI use go after 400 days. Encrypted backups are rotated and the oldest is at most a year old.
privacy.contact: To have your account and everything in it deleted, or to ask anything about this policy, open an issue at <link></link>.

support.title: Support
support.intro: Help with Variater and its Excel add-in: how to ask a question or report a problem, what the add-in does, and what you need to use it.
support.help: To ask a question, report a problem or suggest a change, open an issue at <link></link>. We read every one and answer there.
support.helpPublic: Issues are public, so describe what you did and what you saw, but never paste figures from your deals, your files or anything you would not publish.
support.what: Variater is a modelling tool for investment professionals. Its equity research workspace reads a listed company's published results filing, lets you check every figure beside the page it came from, keeps the quarters you accept, and builds a sector model, a valuation and a results note from them. It drafts; the view, the target and the argument are always yours.
support.whatAddin: The Excel add-in brings that work into your workbook: it signs in to your Variater account, imports a checked quarter as cells with the statement's own sums as formulas and the source page beside each figure, loads a company's sector model as live formulas, reads a results PDF you choose for review, and saves a model you have edited back to Variater.
support.account: The add-in works only with a Variater account. Signing up is free at variater.com, with your email address or Google; it asks for your country and currency first, so make the account on the website before signing in from Excel. The add-in then opens a small window on variater.com to sign in.
support.install: In Excel on Windows, the Mac or the web: Home, Add-ins, search for Variater and choose Add. Then open it from the Home tab.
support.questionGoogle: Google won't sign in inside Excel's window: on Windows and the Mac, Google may refuse to sign in inside an app's own window. Sign in with your email address instead; it is the same account if the address is the same.
support.questionEnded: The add-in asks me to sign in again: its sign-in lasts a working day, and ends at once when you choose Sign out. Signing in again picks up where you were; your workbook keeps every cell it wrote.
support.questionRemove: Removing the add-in: in Excel, open Add-ins, find Variater and remove it. To delete your Variater account and everything in it, open an issue at the address above.
support.privacy: What Variater keeps about you and the add-in, who handles it and how to have it removed is in the <link>privacy policy</link>.

reader.publicConfirm: This is a listed company's published results

reader.stageReadB: Reading the statement pages again (second model)
reader.offBody: This server has no AI provider set up, so it can't read filings.
reader.closedBody: The reader opens here once it has met its accuracy bar on filings nobody tuned it on: no wrong figure left unflagged and under 3% of figures amber.

reader.belowBarBody: Measured on {cases} filings nobody tuned it on ({share} of figures amber), it has not yet met its bar: no wrong figure left unflagged and under 3% of figures amber. Check every figure.
reader.howBody: Upload a quarterly results PDF (Documents keeps it, after its scan). One AI model reads the whole filing and finds the statements; a second, different model reads pictures of those pages again. Every figure the two reads give differently, that fails a sum the statement states, that leaves the balance sheet or the cash flow out of step, that differs from a quarter you already accepted, or that sits on a poorly scanned page without a sum to confirm it, is amber. You then review it with the page beside the figures; nothing is kept until you accept the quarter.

coverage.error_no_read: That read is not yours, or gone.
coverage.error_read_expired: Reads are kept six hours; this one is gone. Read the filing again.
coverage.error_not_found: That company is not in your coverage.
coverage.error_too_many_periods: Your account keeps as many accepted periods as it may. Remove some first.
coverage.error_coverage_full: Coverage storage on this server is full for now.
coverage.error_too_many_companies: You follow as many companies as an account may. Remove one first.

excel.title: Variater for Excel
excel.outsideOffice: This page is the Variater add-in's task pane. Open it from Excel: Home, Add-ins, Variater.
excel.signInHint: Sign in to bring your checked results into this workbook. A window opens to sign in on variater.com.
excel.googleNote: Google may refuse to sign in inside Excel's own window on Windows and Mac. If it does, sign in with your email address instead: it is the same account.
excel.signInClosed: The sign-in window was closed before you signed in.
excel.signInFailed: The sign-in window couldn't open (Office error {code}).
excel.ended: Your add-in sign-in has ended. Sign in again.
excel.noCompanies: No covered companies yet. Add one below, or on variater.com under Coverage.
excel.noPeriods: No accepted quarters for this company yet.
excel.written: Written to {count, plural, one {# sheet} other {# sheets}}: {names}
excel.notesAsComments: This Excel has no notes, so each figure's page is in a comment instead.
excel.noNotes: This Excel holds neither notes nor comments, so the figures' pages are left out; the download has them.
excel.writeFailed: Excel refused the cells. Try again in a new workbook.
excel.modelHint: The model as live formulas, its past filled from the company's accepted quarters. Type the assumptions into the yellow cells: the projection moves in Excel, with no call to Variater. Not yet vetted by a practising analyst.
excel.modelFailed: The model couldn't be written. Try again in a new workbook.
excel.savedHint: On a covered company's model sheet: Save to Variater keeps the yellow assumptions and the constants you typed here; blue figures and formulas stay as Variater holds them. A sheet whose rows or named cells were moved is refused: load the model again. Roll forward moves the model on to newer accepted results and writes it again.
excel.savedBack: {count, plural, =0 {Saved: nothing had changed} one {Saved: # cell changed} other {Saved: # cells changed}}
excel.rolled: Rolled forward to {period}; {lines, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} set beside the estimate, on variater.com under Coverage, Model.
excel.confirmPublic: This is a listed company's published results
excel.amberLeft: {count, plural, =0 {Every amber figure answered} one {# amber figure left} other {# amber figures left}}
excel.connectHint: Sign in as you do on variater.com. This window then hands Excel a sign-in of its own, which reaches your coverage only and lasts a working day.
excel.noAccountHint: No account yet? Create one on variater.com first.
excel.connected: Excel is signed in. This window closes by itself; if it doesn't, close it.
excel.connectError_no_account: Finish your account on variater.com first (country, currency, format and time zone).
excel.connectError_no_database: This server keeps no accounts (no database).
excel.connectError_failed: Excel couldn't be signed in. Close this window and try again.
excel.connectOutsideOffice: This window is opened by the Variater add-in in Excel. Sign in from the add-in's task pane.

models.example_lemon_tree_hotels: Lemon Tree Hotels, solved by hand
models.example_jk_lakshmi_cement: JK Lakshmi Cement, solved by hand
models.addLine: Add a line worked out by
models.places: Costs per place per day, or per unit sold, follow
models.placesNone: No line: costs are a share of revenue
models.block_capacity: Places x share filled x price per day
models.block_subscribers: Subscribers x revenue each, less churn
models.block_people: Headcount x utilisation x billing rate
models.block_plant: Capacity x utilisation x price per unit sold
models.block_stores: Stores x revenue per store per day
models.choice_end_to_date: Line {line}, the count at the end of the part reported
models.choice_value_year: Target multiple: the year it is applied to
models.option_drivers: The drivers are printed: revenue is worked out
models.option_revenue: Revenue is printed: the places in use are worked out
models.option_ev_ebitda: EV/EBITDA: the year's EBITDA, less net debt and non-controlling interests
models.option_pe: P/E: the year's earnings per share
models.workbookHint: The model as live Excel formulas: assumptions are yellow, named cells; change one in Excel and the projection moves with no call to Variater.
models.notVetted: No practising analyst has read this model yet. It is solved by hand for two companies; check it before relying on it.
models.error_model_refused: The model can't be built this way.
models.error_company_refused: A figure or choice doesn't fit the model.
models.error_cannot_work_out: A figure makes a row impossible to work out.
models.error_failed: The model couldn't be worked out. Try again.
models.missing: {count, plural, one {# assumption is} other {# assumptions are}} still blank; the cells that read them stay blank until it is typed.
models.undefined: {count, plural, one {# cell divides} other {# cells divide}} by a figure still blank, so they stay blank.
models.dropped: {count, plural, one {# figure was} other {# figures were}} typed for cells the changed model works out or no longer has, and were left out.
models.fill_nothing_accepted: No accepted quarter of these figures yet: type the past, or accept a quarter under Results first.
models.fill_year_complete: The newest filing is a whole year: it is last year, and the year in progress has nothing reported yet.
models.fill_quarter_missing: A quarter of the year in progress is not accepted, so the part reported is left blank.
models.fill_no_last_year: No accepted filing prints last year whole, so last year is left blank.
models.fill_no_balance_sheet: No accepted filing has last year's balance sheet: type it, from the year-end results.
models.fill_leases_in_finance_costs: Finance costs went into interest on borrowings: the filing does not split out interest on leases.
models.fill_other_currency: A filing in another currency was left out.
models.emptyBody: Start from a sector, filling the past from a covered company's accepted quarters, or open a company the model was solved by hand for.
models.opensSaved: This company has a saved model: it opens as you left it.
models.notSaved: Not saved: an example, or a company not in your coverage. Keep it in coverage to save it as you type, with versions.
models.savedAt: Saved as you type. Latest version: {version}
models.newer: Accepted results now reach {end} ({months} months of the year). Roll the model forward: its lines and assumptions are kept, the past moves on, and this estimate is kept beside the results.
models.rolledQuarter: The months reported are now the new results; the rest of the year keeps its assumptions, so check any typed as amounts for a longer rest of year. {carried, plural, =0 {Nothing was carried} one {# figure was carried from before, marked amber} other {# figures were carried from before, marked amber}}; {toType, plural, =0 {nothing is left to type} one {# figure over the new period is left to type} other {# figures over the new period are left to type}}.
models.rolledYear: Last year is now the year reported, and every assumption moved back a year; the last forecast year repeats the one before, marked amber. {carried, plural, =0 {Nothing was carried} one {# figure was carried from before, marked amber} other {# figures were carried from before, marked amber}}; {toType, plural, =0 {nothing is left to type} one {# figure over the new period is left to type} other {# figures over the new period are left to type}}.
models.basis_share_of_rest_by_days: The estimate is the share by days of {from} as the model stood before the results; the model holds no quarters.
models.basis_year_as_reported: The estimate is {from} as the model stood before the results, against the year as reported.
models.saved_no_as_of: This model was not started from accepted results, so it doesn't know which period it holds. Start it again from the company's results.
models.saved_nothing_newer: The accepted results reach no further than the model.
models.saved_older_results: The accepted results are older than the model.
models.saved_too_far: The accepted results are more than a year past the model. Start the model again from them.
models.saved_no_results: The results for the new period are not all accepted: accept every quarter of the year so far, or the year's results.
models.saved_changed_meanwhile: The model changed while it was rolling forward. Try again.
models.saved_model_too_large: The model is too large to save.
models.saved_too_many_versions: This model holds as many versions as it can.
models.saved_coverage_full: Coverage is full on this server.
models.saved_restructured: The sheet's structure was changed, so it was not saved:
models.saved_not_a_number: A yellow cell holds words, so the sheet was not saved:
models.saved_other_model: This sheet is not a saved Variater model, or not this company's: load the model again.
models.saved_not_found: This model is not in your coverage.
models.saved_failed: The model couldn't be saved. Try again.
models.valuationHow: As at the end of last year: net debt, non-controlling interests and the shares are last year's balance sheet, from the accepted results, and each year's cash flow from the current year on is discounted to it. Type the discount rate, the growth after the forecast, the target multiple and the price with its date in last year's column of the model below; each is a yellow cell in the workbook too.
models.valuationDcf: Value per share, discounted cash flow
models.valuationDcfSub: Discount rate {rate}, growth after the forecast {growth}
models.valuationNoValue: no value until its assumptions are typed
models.valuationTypePrice: Type the price and its date in the model below
models.valuationNoDate: Type the price's date in the model below
models.riskFree_ok: Starting point for the discount rate: {country}'s 10-year government bond yield, {rate} ({period}, {source}). Add the premium you judge right.
models.riskFreeUse: Start the discount rate from it
models.riskFree_no_currency: No risk-free rate to offer: the accepted results are in no single currency yet.
models.riskFree_no_country: No risk-free rate to offer: the results' currency is not one country's we hold figures for.
models.riskFree_no_data: No risk-free rate to offer: no 10-year yield is stored for the results' country.
models.riskFreeCovered: A company kept in coverage is offered its country's 10-year government yield as a starting point.

report.noCompanies: No covered company yet: add one on Coverage → Companies and save a model for it on Coverage → Model.
report.tool: Every number in this note is filled from your saved model and checked against its cell. The view, the target and the argument are yours to type: the tool picks none and leaves them empty until you do.
report.limit: The sentences were written as often as allowed today. Try again tomorrow; the templates write them meanwhile.
report.refused_no_model: This company has no saved model yet. Build one on Coverage → Model; the note is drawn from it.
report.refused_no_version: That version of the model doesn't exist. Pick another one to compare with.
report.refused_not_found: This company isn't in your coverage.
report.refused_figure_differs: A figure didn't match its cell in the model, so the note was not drawn. Reload the page and try again.
report.refused_number_not_from_model: A sentence held a number that is not one of the model's, so the note was not drawn. Write the sentences again.
report.refused_label_differs: A name in the note didn't match the model's, so the note was not drawn. Reload the page and try again.
report.refused_typed_differs: A field you typed didn't come through as typed. Save it again.
report.refused_call_in_text: A sentence held words of a view the tool may not state, so the note was not drawn. Write the sentences again.
report.refused_no_model_values: The model has no revenue to draw a note from.
report.refused_failed: The note couldn't be drawn. Try again in a moment.
report.emptyBody: Pick a covered company with a saved model to see its note.
report.previewLabel: The note as it will be written
report.viewHint: Yours alone: typed here, written into the note as typed, and left empty until you type them.
report.targetInvalid: Type a number of zero or more.
report.sentencesHint: Short sentences joining the tables. The AI is sent only what each figure means and which way it moved, never the company or a figure; the app puts the figures in. A sentence that holds a number or a view is written by its template instead.
report.source_ai_refused: Template: the AI's broke a rule
report.detailsHint: Typed once for every note you draft: your firm's name and the disclosures your regulator requires. Check the wording with your compliance adviser.
report.detailsFailed: Not saved. Check the firm name is at most 200 characters and try again.
report.downloadHint: The note as shown, with native charts in Word. Each download goes in your history.
